clue.text: Register a rapid succession of drumbeats

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an official list, as in an electoral or class register
second meaning: a drum effect of fast repeated strokes

explanation.surface: Someone noting down a drumroll as it happens.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both an official list of names and a continuous fast beating on a drum.

clue.text: Fish below, little Florence above

parts.note: Flo is the short form of the name Florence
a synonym: beneath

explanation.surface: A description of where a fish sits relative to a girl called Florence.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'above' places the first piece on top of the second, so the short name comes before the word for beneath.
explanation.definitionFit: A flounder is a flatfish found in coastal waters.

clue.text: Legal document unaffected by revolution

indicators.note: if turning the word round leaves it unchanged, it reads the same in both directions

parts.note: a signed legal instrument, and it reads the same both ways

explanation.surface: A legal paper that survives a political uprising intact.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolution' suggests political upheaval, but here it means turning the word round: it reads the same backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A deed is a written, signed legal instrument, such as one conveying property.

clue.text: I've chucked in tulip cultivation to paint the town red

indicators.note: something chucked in is tossed into the middle of something else
cultivation works and turns over the soil, so the letters are dug up and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written, without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A gardener announcing they've thrown themselves into growing tulips in order to have fun.
explanation.walkthrough: The three letters go into the flower's name and the whole lot is then rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are idioms for going out and celebrating extravagantly.

clue.text: Sculpture reportedly transported

indicators.note: reportedly means as people say it, so the word is judged by its sound

parts.note: a bust is a sculpture of head and shoulders

explanation.surface: A news item that a statue has been moved somewhere.
explanation.definitionFit: To be bussed is to be carried by bus, a form of being transported.

clue.text: Manage bit of publicity with clergyman

parts.note: an ad is a single advertisement
a minister is a member of the clergy

explanation.surface: Advice to run a church's affairs with a little help from advertising.
explanation.definitionFit: To administer an organisation is to run or direct it.

clue.text: A tantalising person relaxed

parts.note: taken as written
a tease is someone who tantalises others

explanation.surface: A description of a flirt who is calm and unbothered.
explanation.definitionFit: Being at ease means being comfortable and free of tension.

clue.text: Worried gymnast, somewhat nervous

indicators.note: somewhat means only a portion, so the letters come from part of the words before it

parts.note: the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: An anxious gymnast who is a bit jittery before competing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Worried' looks like the definition, but it supplies letters; the definition is 'nervous'.
explanation.definitionFit: Edgy is a common informal synonym for tense or anxious.

clue.text: Hardy dog not needing lead

indicators.note: the lead of a word is its first letter, and not needing it means dropping it

parts.note: a collie is a sheepdog breed

explanation.surface: A tough dog that can be walked without a leash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hardy' looks like an adjective for the dog, but it is Oliver Hardy of Laurel and Hardy, known as Ollie.
explanation.definitionFit: Ollie was the nickname of Oliver Hardy, the comic partner of Stan Laurel.

clue.text: Flooded home — with no indication of when it happened?

parts.note: being in means being at home

parts.words: no indication of when it happened
parts.note: something with no date on it

explanation.surface: A house under water, with nobody sure when the flood came.
explanation.definitionFit: Inundated literally means overwhelmed with water, swamped.

clue.text: Washer of Los Angeles strip

parts.note: the standard abbreviation for the city
to strip is to take off one's clothes

explanation.surface: Someone who cleans a street in Los Angeles, or its team kit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Washer' could be a machine or a plumbing part; here it is a person who washes clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: A laundress is a woman employed to wash and iron clothes and linen.

clue.text: Odd bits missing in rift valley country

indicators.note: losing the odd-numbered positions leaves only the even ones in place

parts.note: the second, fourth, sixth, eighth and tenth letters

explanation.surface: Pieces of land gone from a geological valley somewhere abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: A rift valley sounds like East African geography, which steers the solver away from a European country.
explanation.definitionFit: Italy is a country in southern Europe.

clue.text: Monsieur in rebuilt Ostend terminal

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another
rebuilding puts the same materials together in a new form

parts.note: the Belgian port, taken as written
M is the abbreviation for Monsieur

explanation.surface: A Frenchman at the ferry terminal in the reconstructed Belgian port of Ostend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Terminal' sounds like a ferry building, but it is the adjective meaning at the very end.
explanation.definitionFit: Endmost means furthest along or at the end, as terminal does.

clue.text: We turned up with endless Irish pitchers

indicators.note: endless means the final letter is cut off
in a down clue, turning up flips the word so it reads from the bottom

parts.note: the pronoun, read upwards
Erse is the Irish Gaelic language, here losing its tail

explanation.surface: A sports report: we arrived with Irish bowlers or baseball pitchers.
explanation.walkthrough: Erse is an old name for the Gaelic languages, especially Irish.
explanation.definitionFit: Ewers are large jugs, and pitcher is another name for a jug.

clue.text: Gluttony and anger I veto after reformation

indicators.note: a reformation reshapes something, so these letters are put into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A reformed sinner rejecting the deadly sins of gluttony and anger.
explanation.walkthrough: Gluttony and anger sound like a list of two sins; only the first is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Gluttony is the habit of eating to excess.

clue.text: People on the roads from golf clubs

definitions.meaning: second meaning: the long-distance clubs used to tee off

explanation.surface: Motorists heading home from their golf clubs.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both those who steer vehicles and the woods used for long shots in golf.

clue.text: Express a lack of interest in Welsh rugby?

indicators.note: in means the letters sit inside the following words

parts.note: the end of the first word and start of the second

explanation.surface: Someone who doesn't care about rugby in Wales, where it is a national passion.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the joke that anyone indifferent to Welsh rugby would be rare.
explanation.definitionFit: Lifting the shoulders is the gesture of not caring or not knowing.

clue.text: European leading lady? That is weird!

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for European
ER, Elizabeth Regina, the Queen as the country's first lady
with 'is' it forms 'that is', abbreviated i.e.

explanation.surface: Someone startled to meet a European actress in the lead role.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That is' does double duty in the surface, but only 'That' needs a block; 'is' joins it into i.e.
explanation.definitionFit: Eerie means strange and unsettling, close in sense to weird.

clue.text: Father Ted's capital postman

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father

indicators.note: 'capital' keeps only the first letter of 'Ted'

parts.note: the capital, or first letter, of the name

explanation.surface: A sitcom priest's favourite London postman.
explanation.walkthrough: Father Ted is an Irish sitcom about a priest, a false trail. Postman Pat is a British children's TV postman.
explanation.definitionFit: Postman Pat is the famous children's television postman, so the name stands for the postman.

clue.text: Just Boy George's first potty antiques?

indicators.note: potty means crazy, so the letters go mad and scramble

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: first picks out only the opening letter of the name

parts.note: the initial of the name

explanation.surface: Is Boy George merely a collection of pottery antiques?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Potty' plays on pottery: the answer is a pottery item.
explanation.definitionFit: Toby jugs are collectable ceramic jugs shaped like a seated man in a tricorn hat, often antique.

clue.text: One who won't give up row over river

indicators.note: over here means covering, so one piece is wrapped around the other

parts.note: a tier is a row of seats
R is the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A determined rower battling on the river.
explanation.definitionFit: A trier is someone who keeps making the effort, a persistent person.

clue.text: In names, in titles, in acronyms, letters seen for starters

definitions.text: In names, in titles, in acronyms, letters seen for starters

indicators.note: starters are the opening letters of each word

parts.words: In names, in titles, in acronyms, letters seen
parts.note: the leading letter of each of the eight words

explanation.surface: A description of where we see opening letters used.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines the answer, and its words' first letters also spell it out.
explanation.definitionFit: Initials are the first letters of words, used in names, titles and acronyms.

clue.text: Strident noise made by loose stones in front of church

parts.note: scree is loose rock on a mountainside
CH is the abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: A harsh grinding noise of gravel in front of a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In front of' puts the stones before the church in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A screech is a harsh, shrill cry or sound.

clue.text: Uncover most of red meat

indicators.note: most of means all but the last letter is kept

parts.note: the colour word losing its final letter
veal is calf meat

explanation.surface: Taking the cover off a dish of mostly rare meat.
explanation.definitionFit: To reveal is to expose or disclose, to take the cover off.

clue.text: Youngster's top outlaw, extremely immature

parts.note: a hood is a gangster, short for hoodlum

indicators.note: extremely means the extremes, the outer letters of the word

parts.note: the first and last letters

explanation.surface: A youngster whose top villain is a very childish one.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoodie is a hooded sweatshirt, a top much worn by young people.

clue.text: Part of London heard from Isle of Dogs?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a district of East London
second meaning: the noise dogs make

explanation.walkthrough: The Isle of Dogs is itself a district of East London, so the clue looks purely geographical; the dogs are taken literally.
explanation.definitionFit: Barking is an East London district, and also the sound a dog makes.

clue.text: Joiner in Rhode Island with former GI?

parts.note: the US state abbreviation
a vet is a veteran soldier

explanation.surface: A carpenter living in Rhode Island alongside an ex-soldier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joiner' suggests a carpenter, but it is a metal fastener.
explanation.definitionFit: A rivet is a metal pin used to join plates together.

clue.text: Wading bird under the weather, so we hear

indicators.note: so we hear means the word is judged by its sound

parts.note: feeling rough means feeling unwell

explanation.surface: A report of a sick wading bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The ruff is a Eurasian wading bird known for the male's frilled neck feathers.

clue.text: Detached target

definitions.meaning: first meaning: impartial, not influenced by feelings
second meaning: an aim or goal

explanation.walkthrough: The pair reads like a target on its own, but they are two unrelated senses.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is an adjective for unbiased judgement and a noun for a goal being aimed at.

clue.text: Member of force with unknown ape

parts.note: a cop is a member of the police force
in algebra x, y and z stand for unknowns

explanation.surface: A police officer accompanied by a mysterious gorilla.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ape' looks like a noun for the animal but is the verb meaning imitate.
explanation.definitionFit: To ape someone is to mimic or imitate them.

clue.text: Grub found in wheat sheaf

indicators.note: found in means sitting inside the words that follow

parts.note: the end of the first word and start of the second

explanation.surface: An insect larva discovered inside a bundle of harvested wheat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grub' wants to be a larva; it is slang for food.
explanation.definitionFit: Grub and eats are both informal words for food.

clue.text: Scottish dance interrupted by family member showing off

indicators.note: something interrupted has another thing break into its middle

parts.note: the Highland fling is a Scottish dance
a relative

explanation.surface: A relative cutting in on a Scottish dance to show off.
explanation.definitionFit: Flaunting is displaying something ostentatiously, which is showing off.

clue.text: One-off programme for aviator

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a trial TV episode made to test a series
second meaning: someone who flies aircraft

explanation.surface: A single TV show made about a flyer.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a trial episode of a television series and also a person who flies a plane.
